offshore-wind-coal-taxpayer-funded-rollb.why: The D.C. Circuit vacated DOE's first Campbell coal-plant order as an unlawful use of Federal Power Act emergency power; DOE seeks rehearing and keeps issuing orders.

offshore-wind-coal-taxpayer-funded-rollb.who: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum (U.S. Department of the Interior)
offshore-wind-coal-taxpayer-funded-rollb.why: A judge ruled Interior's suspension of the nearly complete Revolution Wind project "arbitrary and capricious"; courts let all five paused projects resume.

parnell-stars-and-stripes-independence-2.who: Office of the Assistant to the Secretary of Defense for Public Affairs (Sean Parnell)
parnell-stars-and-stripes-independence-2.why: The Defense Department removed Stars and Stripes' editorial-independence rules without notice and comment; a pending readers' suit says the Administrative Procedure Act required it.

patel-bondi-arctic-frost-agents-lawsuit-.who: FBI Director Kash Patel and then-Attorney General Pam Bondi
patel-bondi-arctic-frost-agents-lawsuit-.why: Pending suits allege Patel and Bondi fired career FBI agents over perceived political affiliation tied to their Trump investigations; the government disputes it.

patel-bondi-arctic-frost-agents-lawsuit-.who: FBI Director Kash Patel and then-Attorney General Pam Bondi
patel-bondi-arctic-frost-agents-lawsuit-.why: Pending suits allege the agents were fired without due process; the government argues they were at-will employees with no protected interest in their jobs.

patel-bondi-arctic-frost-agents-lawsuit-.who: FBI Director Kash Patel and then-Deputy Director Dan Bongino
patel-bondi-arctic-frost-agents-lawsuit-.why: A lawsuit alleges Patel or people at his direction, and Bongino, gave Congress Arctic Frost grand jury material without the court authorization Rule 6(e) requires.
A lawsuit alleges Patel falsely told House and Senate committees the firings followed internal investigations; it says none of the fired employees was investigated.

patel-fbi-el-sayed-video-hatch-act-2026.why: The FBI's official X account posted a video attacking Democrats, including Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, weeks before the midterms; CREW says OSC opened a Hatch Act probe.

patel-journalist-retaliation-2025-2026.who: Federal Bureau of Investigation under Director Kash Patel
patel-journalist-retaliation-2025-2026.why: The FBI reportedly looked into a Times reporter after her story on Patel's girlfriend's security; some DOJ officials saw it as retaliation with no legal basis.

pentagon-civilian-harm-reduction-program.why: The Pentagon's inspector general found the dismantled program left the military without the personnel, tools or infrastructure needed to comply with the two statutes that require it.

pentagon-civilian-workforce-cuts-no-anal.why: GAO found DOD components did not consistently do the impact analysis federal law requires before civilian workforce cuts, including 2025's deferred resignations, as DOD shed about 78,000 jobs.

pulte-mortgage-data-misuse-2025-2026.who: Bill Pulte, Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency
pulte-mortgage-data-misuse-2025-2026.why: Rep. Eric Swalwell sued, alleging Pulte violated the Privacy Act by accessing his mortgage records for political purposes; the suit was dismissed without prejudice.

pulte-mortgage-data-misuse-2025-2026.who: Bill Pulte, Acting Director of National Intelligence
pulte-mortgage-data-misuse-2025-2026.why: A Cato Institute legal analysis says Pulte exceeded his acting authority by continuing to act as DNI, including firing staff, for about a week after Clayton's confirmation.
FHFA's inspector general reported FHFA refused records it requested, calling that unprecedented and citing its right to all records; FHFA disputes the account.

rfk-jr-acip-apa-violation-2026-03.who: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Secretary of Health and Human Services
rfk-jr-acip-apa-violation-2026-03.why: A federal judge preliminarily ruled plaintiffs were likely to show the ACIP overhaul and January 2026 schedule changes violated the APA, and stayed them; an appeal is pending.

rfk-jr-acip-apa-violation-2026-03.who: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Secretary of Health and Human Services
rfk-jr-acip-apa-violation-2026-03.why: A judge held plaintiffs plausibly alleged the reconstituted ACIP does not comport with FACA requirements, denying dismissal; the suit is pending.

rfk-jr-samoa-vaccine-testimony-2026.who: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., HHS Secretary
rfk-jr-samoa-vaccine-testimony-2026.why: Kennedy told senators his Samoa trip had nothing to do with vaccines, though his own 2019 letter proposed assessing Samoa's MMR vaccines; a watchdog asked DOJ to investigate.

rollins-establishment-clause-2026-05.why: USDA employees sued, alleging Rollins's department-wide Christian messages are unconstitutionally coercive; the emails may violate the Establishment Clause.

rosen-don-lemon-church-protest-prosecuti.who: Daniel Rosen, U.S. Attorney for the District of Minnesota
rosen-don-lemon-church-protest-prosecuti.why: Lemon has moved to dismiss the charges as vindictive prosecution; the district's chief judge had written there was no evidence he engaged in criminal behavior.

rubio-state-dept-mass-visa-revocations-2.why: After a trial, a federal judge found Rubio implemented a policy "in a viewpoint-discriminatory way to chill protected speech"; a second judge ruled for speech plaintiffs; both on appeal.
A federal judge ruled the speech-based visa enforcement policy also violated the APA and vacated it; the ruling is on appeal.

rubio-vacancies-act-concentration-2025-2.why: NARA and GAO confirmed the Archivist vacancy was not reported to GAO until Jan. 23, 2026, over seven weeks after Rubio's stated exit, which may breach the Act's reporting requirement.

sonderling-imls-unlawful-actions-2025.who: Keith Sonderling, Acting Director of IMLS
sonderling-imls-unlawful-actions-2025.why: A federal court in Rhode Island found the IMLS dismantling actions he carried out, including staff cuts and grant cancellations, arbitrary and capricious and contrary to law.

trump-cnn-msnow-politico-white-house-ban.who: Donald Trump, President, and White House officials
trump-cnn-msnow-politico-white-house-ban.why: A federal judge preliminarily enjoined the revocation of CNN, MS NOW and Politico hard passes, finding the outlets likely to win First Amendment retaliation claims; DOJ is appealing.

trump-cnn-msnow-politico-white-house-ban.who: Donald Trump, President, and White House officials
trump-cnn-msnow-politico-white-house-ban.why: The same judge found the outlets likely to win their Fifth Amendment due-process claim because the passes were revoked without notice or a chance to be heard.

trump-dc-police-federal-takeover-2025.why: Judge Jia Cobb ruled the Guard deployment likely unlawful as an intrusion on D.C. officials' authority over local law enforcement; an appeals court stayed that ruling while the appeal is pending.
D.C.'s attorney general sued, alleging Guard troops deputized for armed patrols are being used for law enforcement in possible violation of the Posse Comitatus Act; the suit is pending.

trump-election-eo-14248-military-voters-.why: Courts permanently blocked parts of the order, one writing that the Constitution "assigns no authority to the president over federal election administration"; appeals pending.

trump-gender-affirming-care-eo-2025.who: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
trump-gender-affirming-care-eo-2025.why: A federal judge vacated HHS's 'Kennedy Declaration,' cited to justify the restrictions, ruling it exceeded HHS's statutory authority; HHS has appealed.

trump-gender-affirming-care-eo-2025.who: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
trump-gender-affirming-care-eo-2025.why: A federal judge ruled HHS's 'Kennedy Declaration' violated federal notice-and-comment rulemaking requirements and vacated it; HHS has appealed.

trump-inspectors-general-mass-firing-202.why: A judge wrote it is 'obvious' that Trump violated the Inspector General Act by firing 17 inspectors general without the 30 days' notice and reasons owed to Congress.

trump-iran-war-powers-resolution-2026.why: He kept U.S. forces in the Iran war, begun without authorization, past the law's 60-day limit and a June concurrent resolution to withdraw; he says hostilities ended in April.

trump-kennedy-center-injunction-violatio.who: Kennedy Center board of trustees, chaired by Donald Trump
trump-kennedy-center-injunction-violatio.why: Judge Cooper ruled that only Congress can rename the Kennedy Center and ordered Trump's name removed after the Trump-chaired board voted to rename it without congressional authorization.

trump-kennedy-center-injunction-violatio.who: Kennedy Center board of trustees, chaired by Donald Trump
trump-kennedy-center-injunction-violatio.why: Judge Cooper held that the board's planned Trump inscription and plaza renaming violate his naming injunction ("bucks a federal court order") and blocked both; he made no contempt finding.

trump-krebs-security-clearance-doj-inves.why: Trump's memo revoked Krebs's clearances and ordered a DOJ/DHS probe, faulting him for denying the 2020 election was "rigged and stolen"; elements of possible retaliation for protected speech.

trump-maga-inc-super-pac-control-2026.who: Donald Trump, President, and MAGA Inc.
trump-maga-inc-super-pac-control-2026.why: Trump says he controls MAGA Inc. and decides its spending; a Campaign Legal Center FEC complaint alleges he directed soft money that MAGA Inc. raised, with no FEC finding.

trump-mail-ballot-eo-usps-voter-list-rul.who: U.S. Postal Service under Postmaster General David Steiner
trump-mail-ballot-eo-usps-voter-list-rul.why: A federal judge ruled that Congress never delegated its Elections Clause power to the Postal Service and blocked its mail-ballot rule; the Supreme Court left that block in place.
A federal judge declared two sections of the mail-ballot order void as ultra vires; the Supreme Court paused that ruling on whether states could sue yet, not on legality.

trump-mail-ballot-eo-usps-voter-list-rul.who: U.S. Postal Service under Postmaster General David Steiner
trump-mail-ballot-eo-usps-voter-list-rul.why: A federal judge found the Postal Service "feigned compliance" with her injunction by issuing its final rule anyway; she declined to block the rule and later canceled that injunction.

trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.who: OMB and DHS (Customs and Border Protection)
trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.why: Judges in New York and Washington found challengers likely to show that OMB's $20 million apportionment and DHS's ad buy violated the APA, a claim the government did not defend on the merits.

trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.who: OMB and DHS (Customs and Border Protection)
trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.why: About $19 million in CBP money may have paid to air ads for propaganda purposes; a New York judge found challengers likely to succeed on this claim, which the government did not contest.

trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.who: OMB and DHS (Customs and Border Protection)
trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.why: CBP money Congress gave for commemorative events paid to air the ads, possibly misusing it; a New York judge found challengers likely to succeed on this claim, which the government did not contest.

trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.who: Executive Office of the President, OMB and DHS
trump-taxpayer-funded-pro-trump-ads-2026.why: A New York judge found challengers likely to succeed on their ultra vires claim as to three of the ads and barred their dissemination, ordering them off government websites.

usaid-dismantlement-trump2.why: A pending class action by USAID workers alleges Elon Musk and DOGE dismantled USAID without Senate-confirmed authority, which may violate the Appointments Clause.

usda-mass-firings-inspection-collapse-20.why: A judge ruled the Office of Personnel Management's directive behind the probationary firings, including at USDA, was unlawful, but declined to order reinstatement.

usip-doge-takeover-trump2.why: A judge ruled the President's removal of USIP's board unlawful and voided the takeover; an appeals court largely stayed that ruling, finding USIP "exercises substantial executive power."

va-mass-firings-early-2025.why: A judge ruled OPM lacked authority to direct the probationary firings, including at the VA, and ordered records corrected but no rehiring; the government's appeal is pending.

va-warrior-independence-center-unfunded-.why: A judge's housing order, largely upheld on appeal, rests on a finding that VA violated the Rehabilitation Act; the order is paused while VA weighs a Supreme Court petition.

vasquez-perdomo-noem-la-racial-profiling.why: A judge held the government in civil contempt in July 2026, finding by clear and convincing evidence it failed to image agents' phones as ordered; it disputes the personal-phone part.
A pending class action alleges agents stopped people by race, language and job without reasonable suspicion; the Supreme Court paused an order against the stops.

voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.who: Kari Lake, Senior Adviser to the President and former acting CEO of USAGM
voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.why: A judge ruled Kari Lake unlawfully ran USAGM, citing the Federal Vacancies Reform Act, and voided her actions there, including the August 2025 layoffs.

voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.who: Kari Lake, Senior Adviser to the President and former acting CEO of USAGM
voa-usagm-dismantlement-trump2.why: The same ruling cited the Constitution's Appointments Clause in finding an unlawful effort to make Lake USAGM's CEO "in all but name" and voiding her actions.
A judge vacated USAGM's memorandum cutting VOA to a statutory minimum as arbitrary and capricious; an appeals court paused his order returning staff to work.

vought-impoundment-control-act-2025-2026.who: Russell Vought, Director of the Office of Management and Budget
vought-impoundment-control-act-2025-2026.why: GAO found the administration's withholding of funds Congress approved violated the Impoundment Control Act in seven decisions; Vought, who directed it at OMB, calls the law unconstitutional.

wiles-ap-press-access-2025.who: Susie Wiles, White House Chief of Staff
wiles-ap-press-access-2025.why: A judge granted AP a preliminary injunction, finding it was excluded over its Stylebook's viewpoint; an appeals panel stayed it except for the East Room while the appeal is pending.

wright-faca-violation-2026.who: Chris Wright, Secretary of Energy, and the U.S. Department of Energy
wright-faca-violation-2026.why: A federal judge ruled that DOE's Climate Working Group was a federal advisory committee whose FACA violations were "established as matter of law."
A pending lawsuit alleges DOE appointees used personal email to conduct the climate working group's business, which may violate the Federal Records Act.

zeldin-dissent-letter-retaliation-2025-2.who: Lee Zeldin, Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency
zeldin-dissent-letter-retaliation-2025-2.why: Fired probationary EPA staff sued, alleging their firings for signing a personal-capacity dissent letter violated the First Amendment; an EPA lawyer called the letter likely protected speech.
